title: Renewal usage trajectory and ratecap runbook
body:
Purpose: Quick, actionable worksheet CS reps can bring to QBRs to explain recent token velocity, forecast runway, and present a concrete rate-cap/alerting remediation plan tied to renewal asks.

Scope: mid-size accounts (monthly spend $2k-$50k). Focus on token spend patterns, rate-limit incidents, burst behavior, and budget alert sanity checks. Not a billing/legal doc — complementary to finance workbook.

One-line summary (for slide): Token velocity has averaged +38% QoQ with 2 short rate-cap events; recommended immediate actions: set dynamic rate-limit tiers, introduce budget alert at 70% runway, and propose a Dedicated/Commitment talk if projection >80% of committed tokens.

Data inputs (columns to pull into a sheet):
- date_range: string (e.g., 2026-01-01..2026-01-31)
- daily_tokens: numeric daily total tokens consumed
- avg_tokens_per_request: numeric (tokens/request)
- p50_latency_ms: numeric
- rate_limit_hits: integer (count of 429s or throttles)
- distinct_endpoints: integer (routes used)
- top_3_routes_by_tokens: string list
- user_agent_signatures: string list (to identify bots, SDKs)
- invoice_spend_usd: numeric
- committed_tokens (if on Dedicated): numeric

Key KPIs and formulas (in-sheet formulas):
- 7day_MA_tokens = AVERAGE(last 7 days of daily_tokens)
- velocity_delta = (today_7day_MA - prior_7day_MA) / prior_7day_MA
- runway_days = (remaining_budget_tokens) / today_7day_MA
- ratecap_event_rate = rate_limit_hits / number_of_api_minutes_in_window
- anomaly_score (simple) = zscore(daily_tokens over 30d)

Thresholds (recommendations — adjust per account):
- Budget alert levels: 50% (inform), 70% (actionable), 90% (contract escalation)
- Rate-limit severity: low (1-5 hits/day), medium (5-50), high (50+)
- Velocity trigger: sustained >25% week-over-week for 2 consecutive weeks

Suggested alert actions (automation playbook):
1) At 70% budget: Auto-send email to billing contact + create CS ticket. Include 14-day runway estimate and top-3 consuming routes.
2) On medium rate-limit (5-50/day): Throttle non-critical routes via per-route policy, message customer about SDK update with retry/backoff guidance.
3) On high rate-limit (50+): Open immediate SRE ticket, recommend short-term burst credit or temporary increased rate limit; schedule emergency sync.

Escalation matrix (who to loop in):
- CS Rep (owner) — first contact; Slack PM channel #cs-notices
- Solutions Eng — if changes to routing/SDK required; tag @solutions-eng-oncall
- Finance Lead — when 90% alert fires or predicted overage >$5k
- Sales/Account Exec — when runway <14 days or renewal approaching in 30 days

QBR talking points (structure):
- Context: 30d token trend, p95 latency, number of rate-limit events
- What happened: spike patterns (time-of-day, route-level), root cause hypotheses (bot, background job, new feature)
- Impact: user-facing errors, failed integrations, potential cost overrun
- Mitigation we did: throttles, disabling non-essential routes, SDK guidance, applied burst credit
- Proposal: short-term (rate-limit tuning, alerting), medium (commit/discount conversation), long-term (Dedicated or capacity plan + observability add-on)

Sample visuals to include in QBR:
- Rolling 7-day token velocity with annotated spikes
- Heatmap by hour-of-day * route showing consistent batch jobs
- Cumulative spend vs committed tokens with runway bands colored (green/yellow/red)
- Rate-limit events timeline overlayed with deploys or SDK version updates

Example quick SQL snippets (BigQuery style) to populate sheet:
- daily tokens: SELECT DATE(timestamp) as day, SUM(tokens) as daily_tokens FROM `redwood-prod.logs` WHERE customer_id = 'ACME' AND timestamp BETWEEN @start AND @end GROUP BY day ORDER BY day;
- top routes: SELECT route, SUM(tokens) as tokens FROM `redwood-prod.logs` WHERE customer_id='ACME' AND DATE(timestamp) BETWEEN @start AND @end GROUP BY route ORDER BY tokens DESC LIMIT 10;
- rate limit hits: SELECT DATE(timestamp) as day, COUNT(1) as rate_limit_hits FROM `redwood-prod.errors` WHERE customer_id='ACME' AND error_code IN ('429','RATE_LIMIT') AND timestamp BETWEEN @start AND @end GROUP BY day ORDER BY day;

Action checklist for CS rep before QBR:
- Pull last 90d data and compute KPIs above
- Validate top-3 routes with Solutions Eng (are any new?)
- Check billing ledger for pending invoices or credits
- Draft 2 renewal scenarios: conservative (maintain current plan), expansion (commit 30% more tokens), protective (add alerting + cadence to revisit)
- Prepare ask slide with clear success metrics (latency <=200ms, rate-limit hits <5/month, runway >45 days)

Common playbook snippets (copy/paste into customer email):
- "We observed a sustained increase in token usage driven by route X; to avoid unexpected throttles we recommend activating tiered rate-limits and a 70% budget alert so we can proactively manage spend. Can we schedule a 30-minute ops sync this week to review proposed thresholds?"
- "Short term we can provision a 7-day burst allowance to avoid user impact while we tune SDK retries — this requires approval and will be reflected on the next invoice."

Unresolved questions / discussion items: 
- Are spike sources attributable to legitimate traffic (feature) vs. runaway jobs/bots? Need sampling of user_agent and request payloads.
- What's the account's tolerance for automated throttling vs manual intervention?

Notes to self (rep):
- When in doubt, err on conservative runway estimate for renewals. Finance prefers to see proactive mitigation.
- Attach the token-velocity graph exported as PNG and include link to live Grafana.

Appendix: sample Slack escalation template
- Subject: [CS ALERT] ACME — High Rate-limit Events (50+/24h)
- Body: "Hi team — We detected >50 rate-limit events for ACME in the last 24h. Top route: /v1/generate. Customer reports intermittent 429s. Proposed mitigation: temporary route throttle + burst credit. Linking logs: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/usage/token-velocity-dashboard?var-customer=ACME. Please advise within 2 hours."

Revision log: 
- 2025-11-04 initial draft by MT
- 2026-01-08 added SQL snippets and alert thresholds (Ben Carter)
- 2026-02-28 updated escalation matrix and playbook wording after pilot with 3 accounts (Priya Nair)

Open items for product: allow per-route dynamic rate-limit policies and API for temporary burst credits (filed product request: PRD-3149).

End of worksheet.
